lane: fault-zone anatomy: secondary strands around known faults from shear-zone mechanics
hypothesis: A new fault is not a continuation of a mapped trace but a *secondary strand* in the damage zone around it. Its probability therefore factorises into (a) distance to the primary trace, (b) the primary's length as a displacement proxy, and (c) the orientation of the candidate strand relative to the primary strike -- and, critically, (d) whether the pixel actually *carries the geophysical signature of a fault* (magnetic tilt-angle / gravity-gradient edge, detrended-elevation scarp, conductivity and strain contrasts) rather than being a bare distance halo. Term (d) is new this session: the official 19-band GeoDAWN stack was absent from every earlier session of this repository.
mechanism: Damage-zone width grows with displacement (Savage & Brodsky, JGR 2011) and secondary-fracture density decays away from the primary; distributed dextral shear produces en echelon Riedel strands at a relative strike the data, not a textbook, must supply. No angle is hard-coded: every weight is fitted by gradient boosting on the hide-and-recover holdout, and only the measured relative-strike and distance structure is retained.
named_non_fault_process_that_could_mimic: Lithologic contrast and basin-bounding structures. The magnetic tilt-angle, gravity-gradient and conductivity edges that make up the strand-expression term are equally produced by contacts between rock units of different susceptibility or conductivity, by alluvial-basin edges and by the detrended-elevation scarps of erosional topography -- none of which is a fault. Because the training labels are withheld *catalogue* pixels, the model will happily learn 'looks like a mapped fault' from these non-fault edges, so the strand-expression term may be ranking lithology rather than shear.

verdict_detail: NEGATIVE AS A SUBMISSION CANDIDATE, POSITIVE AS A SCIENTIFIC RESULT. The geological hypothesis is supported: strand expression added to lane geometry raises HOLDOUT-DTI from 0.1024 to 0.1103 on the same folds, and the fitted emission is the best the model can produce. But the emission is blocked by protocol rule 1 as written: more than 70% of its dots fall within 3 px of r13-lattice-s5, so the rule's own prescribed action is 'log it as a duplicate and stop'. That clause is measured to be unsatisfiable by any nonempty dot set -- this session found the same obstruction independently of the certificate already on main (17GEMSDOE E-proba-multiscale, positive over the whole allowed domain, forward overlap 1.0 for every candidate). An earlier session of this repository explicitly recorded that the remedy is an owner protocol revision, and NOT a quiet redefinition of support, an exemption for dense maps, a reverse-overlap condition, or picking another raster after STOP. This run therefore reports the obstruction and does not claim an exemption.
remedy_required: owner decision: revise rule 1's directed-overlap clause (or declare the dense/lattice priors out of scope for it), then re-run the screen. This run does not attempt either.
